_comment: Measured pool sizes, read from the token caches on the pod (/data00/tokens_<domain>.pt).
This is the launch gate's epochs prerequisite: gate_epochs_measured refuses any domain
whose epochs came from a stamp estimate rather than a real cache.
HOW: rows = cache.numel() // (SEQ+1), pool_rows = rows - min(int(rows*0.05), 5000).
Both lines are train.py's, not a reimplementation -- _domain_seqs does the first
(n = len(data) // (Cfg.seq+1); data[:n*(seq+1)].view(-1, seq+1)) and the val split
takes seqs[:n_val]. A pool is what remains after the holdout.
WHY IT MATTERS THAT THESE ARE ROWS. A stamp gives tokens; a pool is packed rows, and
they are not proportional -- each document loses a partial row to packing. cot: 424.1M
tokens is 3.83 'epochs' by tokens and 4.03 by rows, i.e. opposite sides of the 4-epoch
line. build_mix draws rows, so rows is the number that decides.
chat_qa and chatml have no cache of their own yet. chat's cache is the same 160,414
documents in plain form and measures 38,187,650 tokens -- exactly the stamp, which
independently confirms the stamp counts ids+<eos> and 3b's bare-ids figure did not.
Their pool_rows below are DERIVED from their stamps by the same formula, and labelled
as such: the number is honest about being one step short of measured.

code_py_rp1t.note: the ast.parse-surviving Python subset; /data00/tokens_code_rp1t.pt holds the FULL 7.57B multi-language corpus (1,847,469 rows), not this subset, so its cache cannot be read for this domain

chat_qa.note: chat/'s cache measures exactly 38,187,650 tokens and 9,320 rows for the same 160,414 documents; chat_qa is a re-render into its own directory and has no cache yet

chatml.note: no cache yet; awaiting pretokenize of data/corpus/chatml/
